chunks: And from him, from them, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Verily, when Allah, the Exalted, created Adam (peace be upon him), He looked at his back and inhaled from it a light, and He created from it the Prophets and the Imams (peace be upon them).'

That light continued to circulate in his loins until the light of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) emerged from it, then the light of Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) emerged, then the light of Hasan (peace be upon him) emerged, then the light of Husayn (peace be upon him) emerged, then the light of the Imams (peace be upon them) emerged.
They are the Light of Allah on earth, and they are the Security of Allah on earth. Whoever encounters them has encountered Allah, and whoever does not encounter them has not encountered Allah.
ai.seo_question: How are the Imams connected to the light of Adam and Allah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq utilizes this hadith to articulate the Shia doctrine of *Nur Muhammad* (the Light of Muhammad), positing that the Imams are the primordial spiritual essence from which all creation emanates. This narrative reinforces the concept of *Isma* (infallibility) by linking the Imams' ontological purity directly to Adam, thereby establishing their recognition (*Ma'rifa*) as the essential key to recognizing Allah. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the Imamate not merely as a political succession but as a continuous divine light guiding humanity.
